#1791 THE Store's own app catalogue: ONE row per package, the single list every Search > Phone page filters (nothing per page). Replaces the three per-page lists (data/fleet/store-phone-recommendations.json, games-catalogue.json, store-play-integrity.json; the first and last are kept only as snapshots of the migration, games-catalogue.json is still read by Cloud Media Center). Bundled in libs:appstore as a tier-4 static seed (runtime-data baseline seed_allowlist) so the pages are never empty while a runtime dataset is unserved; declared for the app in ac_cloud-store/build.json::store_catalogue. Add or correct a row to change a page: no Kotlin, and the filter chips are the `filters` below (id, label, values), so a new value is data too.
FIELDS. category: tools | services | others | games. licence: open | closed (free software or not). play_integrity: none | basic | mid | full (the Play Integrity verdict tier the app is known to need). game_dimension: 2d | 3d, games only (absent elsewhere). source: fdroid | aurora | playstore | other (where the Store gets the APK). icon: an https image URL (or a bundled one), loaded with a disk cache; a generated letter tile is drawn if it fails. Every row also keeps the fields it had in its old list: name, pkg, developer, desc, genre, store_url, apk, basis, note.
RENAMED (so the new field names mean the new thing, no value lost): the old per-list `category` (web, comm, ... / action, adventure, ...) is now `subcategory` (declared in `subcategories`); the old recommendation `licence` (SPDX id, e.g. GPL-3.0) is `licence_spdx`; the old `source` (fdroid | play | github, the listing store) is `source_listed`; the old `open_source` boolean is `licence` open | closed; the old `dimension` is `game_dimension`; the old integrity `tier` is `integrity_tier` (basic | device | strong | unknown, verbatim). `name_integrity_list` holds an integrity-list name that differs from the games-list name of the same package.
CATEGORY MAPPING of the old recommendation categories: web, comm, net, maps -> services (apps that front an online service); files, security, tools, stores -> tools (on-device utilities); media, read -> others; games -> games. Every games-catalogue row is games; every integrity-only row (banks, wallets, payments, exchanges, streaming, Garmin Connect) is services.
PLAY INTEGRITY MAPPING: basic -> basic; device -> mid (MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY); strong -> full (MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY); none = no known requirement. An app the old integrity list marked `unknown` (it is listed because it is expected to attest, but nobody recorded the tier) is rounded to the FLOOR tier `basic`, never to `none`, so a bank is never shown under "No Play"; `play_integrity_basis` says how sure the value is (publisher-documented | reported | unverified | not-on-play) and `integrity_tier` keeps the old verbatim tier, so unknown is not silently lost. A Play game with no record is `none` with basis unverified (no evidence of a requirement); a non-Play app (F-Droid, GitHub) is `none` with basis not-on-play.
SOURCE MAPPING: fdroid and izzy -> fdroid; github -> other (GitHub releases); play -> aurora for the games-catalogue rows (the Store installs a Play game through Aurora's anonymous session first, PlayAnon, then the Play listing) and playstore for the integrity-only rows (bank, wallet and payment apps need the Play account/region, Aurora's anonymous session may be refused, so they go through the Play Store itself); a Play-listed row keeps `source_listed` play whichever of the two it is.
ICONS: games keep their store listing image; F-Droid apps use https://f-droid.org/repo/<pkg>/en-US/icon.png; the few apps without that file use their Play listing image or their project site's favicon (google s2); two UK banks not on the US Play listing use their site favicon. CI checks each URL is https and (when dispatched) resolves.

play_integrity_tiers.label: No Play
play_integrity_tiers.meaning: No known Play Integrity requirement (not on Play, or no evidence of one).

play_integrity_tiers.label: Play Basic
play_integrity_tiers.meaning: Runs on a device that passes only the basic system-integrity check (may be rooted or unlocked-bootloader, but not obviously tampered).

play_integrity_tiers.label: Play Mid
play_integrity_tiers.meaning: Needs a genuine, Play-certified Android device with a locked, uncompromised system.

play_integrity_tiers.label: Play Full
play_integrity_tiers.meaning: Needs a hardware-backed verdict: certified device, locked bootloader and a recent security patch.
